dramatic_truth: Greg identifies earning power as his current highest-leverage lane without demoting magic, body, people, artifacts or adventure into irrelevance.
performance: He refuses unfocused training, seeks narrow institutional proof of work he actually completed, accepts verification rather than praise and uses one field reference to unlock a better-paying custody witness job.
screenplay: Leverage audit; district chain receipt verified; Bracken report timing noted but not certified; transfer-seal witness job taken; mismatched seals and crate marks preserved rather than explained away; second work reference earned.
prose_comparison: The systems reflection pays off immediately in changed earning access. It is strategy tied to action, not abstract optimization monologue.

dramatic_truth: Seven-copper work reveals that increasing earning ceiling means building credible pathways and references, not merely chasing the highest number on a board.
performance: Greg evaluates the next contract for what it unlocks, keeps narrow claims around custody/discrepancy work and remains willing to revise the leverage plan when better evidence appears.
screenplay: Two-reference access produces a higher-tier review opportunity; Greg works the new lane; evidence and pay widen future eligibility rather than instantly making him rich.
prose_comparison: The chapter advances the employment ladder rather than repeating contract shopping.

dramatic_truth: At Cinder Cross Greg confronts a high-paying illegal shortcut and proves the money strategy is not permission to sell judgment.
performance: He prices legal access, hears the illegal offer without moral panic, identifies the actual risk and finds a lawful side door that preserves upside without pretending danger is virtue.
screenplay: Five-copper legal route contrasted with much richer illegal offer; terms and consequences narrowed; Greg refuses the bad lane and locates a legitimate alternative.
prose_comparison: The comparison is the first real stress test of the earning-power strategy and is not redundant financial caution.

dramatic_truth: Sourcing East Fen glass lets Greg create value by connecting specialist supply to demand without needing to own either expertise or inventory.
performance: He verifies the glassyard exists, keeps maker/seller knowledge with its owners, structures the connection and allows payment to move through the system without physically controlling every step.
screenplay: Glass source located; requirements and counterparties aligned; terms travel between specialists; fee/value begins moving independently of Greg's physical presence.
prose_comparison: This is a material shift from labor income to intermediary leverage and deserves its procedural detail.

dramatic_truth: Greg coordinates people for the first time as an economic function and learns that management works better when scope and ownership are explicit than when authority is performed.
performance: He tells people what result and handoff he needs, avoids pretending to own their craft and prices his organizing contribution without turning the group into subordinates.
screenplay: Multiple specialists/workers must align; Greg structures sequence and handoffs; friction appears around who owns what; the job moves because boundaries are clear enough.
prose_comparison: Repeated coordination language is the behavior change itself and should remain visible.

dramatic_truth: Thirteen silver gives Greg enough capital to participate seriously in an auction while still leaving many desirable assets beyond rational reach.
performance: He distinguishes capacity from permission, sets ceilings, values deployability and lets 'not enough' become a directional planning fact rather than humiliation.
screenplay: Substantially larger purse; auction opportunities with real strategic utility; bids/prices test capital discipline; Greg leaves with clearer scale rather than a protagonist bargain.
prose_comparison: The auction repeats the form but not the state: Greg is now capital-constrained at a much higher tier, which is the point.

dramatic_truth: Greg spends five copper simply to go west, letting the road itself produce the value instead of demanding every journey pay financially.
performance: He buys the route, observes what changes around him and permits an uneventful paid passage to count as worthwhile movement.
screenplay: Westbound fare paid; ordinary transit; new route knowledge and perspective accumulate; no forced incident turns the ticket into a plot coupon.
prose_comparison: The quiet travel beat is contrast after intense capital strategy and keeps adventure from becoming only monetized opportunity.

dramatic_truth: A delayed home letter finally converts abstract return optionality into a direct relationship request: if Greg is coming back, he needs to actually come back.
performance: He reads the message without defensiveness, distinguishes pressure from control and decides home now instead of optimizing one more road or job.
screenplay: Letter waiting under his name; accumulated distance and delayed communication become explicit; home asks for action rather than another update; Greg commits to return.
prose_comparison: The letter is earned by the long communication lag and changes the governing priority immediately.

dramatic_truth: Greg pays six copper to come home and discovers that return has value independent of whether the trip can be justified as profitable or complete.
performance: He buys the ticket without bargaining the choice away, lets travel reverse direction and arrives ready to re-enter relationships rather than present a victory report.
screenplay: Home fare paid; west/south travel; familiar geography returns; arrival converts Carrow from compass point back into lived place.
prose_comparison: The return mirrors earlier fares deliberately, but the meaning has reversed from escape/expansion to chosen belonging.

dramatic_truth: Back home, Greg re-enters the work-limb process as a wearer with months of field data rather than the candidate who left Duskport.
performance: He brings real route, surface, fatigue and skin experience back to Hark & Venn, accepts that the fitting must incorporate changed body use and keeps crutches as part of the final mobility system.
screenplay: Hark & Venn note remains at home; Greg returns to fitting dialogue; road-test evidence is reviewed; the limb arc resumes from accumulated use rather than restarting.
prose_comparison: The fitting repetition is payoff to the entire travel experiment because the evidence set is fundamentally different now.
